findings.title: The CLI judge path in Value, Success Criterion 3 and walkthrough step 3 cannot work without engine changes
findings.description:
The Value section (lines 31-35), Functional Requirement 3 (lines 277-282) and walkthrough step 3 (lines 361-368) say `sq review` can run `judge.slice-vs-arch` and return a threshold-derived verdict with `provenance == "judge"`. The current CLI cannot do this:
- There is no `slice-vs-arch` subcommand and no `--template` option. `review_slice` passes the hard-coded name `"slice"` to `_run_review_command`.
- The CLI path calls `run_review_with_profile` directly, not `ReviewAction`. So `enforce_judge()` never runs and `provenance` is never set. A judge template run this way would always persist the parsed verdict, which is `UNKNOWN` because the prompt forbids a `## Summary` line, and the CLI would exit 0.

The note at lines 376-379 treats this as uncertainty about argument shape only. It is really a missing integration path. Meeting criterion 3 as written needs CLI changes: a template option or subcommands, plus enforcement on the CLI path. That contradicts the "one required code change" scope at lines 51-57 and the slice plan's "no engine changes" rule. The task breakdown would inherit a criterion it cannot pass.

**Fix:** Drop the CLI claims and verify end to end through a pipeline `review` step (`sq run`), which does go through `ReviewAction` and enforcement. The slice plan's criterion ("produces a score, derived verdict, and findings, persisted like any review output") is met that way. Record CLI judge support as Future Work.

findings.title: The structured-output constraint assigned to this slice is dropped without saying so
findings.description:
The architecture (Technical Considerations, item (b)) commits that "the judge template uses a structured-output constraint for the score field." The slice plan entry for 302 repeats this. Its success criteria include "The score-with-rationale shape is enforced by the template's structured output." The parser also defers to this slice: `_extract_criteria`'s docstring says "The structured-output/JSON variant is slice 302."

The design instead uses prompt instructions plus the lenient markdown `score:` line, and never mentions structured output. Templates currently have no output-schema mechanism, so delivering this would probably need an engine change. That is a legitimate reason to defer, but the design has to say so. As written, it drops slice-plan scope with no record.

**Fix:** Either specify the structured-output mechanism, or add a Technical Decision that defers it with that reason, and add it to the slice plan's Future Work. Then state which success criterion stands in for it here.

findings.title: Concrete example numbers in the prompt shape invite the anchoring this slice is meant to reduce
findings.description:
The architecture asks for score-with-rationale specifically "to reduce anchoring," and lists "anchoring on the prompt" as a known weakness. The output-shape example (lines 161-178, also 129-133) uses real values: `score: 82`, `alignment: 85`, `scope: 80`. If an implementer copies this example into the system prompt, the model gets an anchor near the pass floors. This is the same hallucination trap the project's CLAUDE.md warns about.

**Fix:** Require the shape example in each template's system prompt to use placeholders that are clearly not values, such as `score: <integer 0-100>` and `<criterion>: <integer 0-100>`. Make this a checkable item under Special Considerations.

findings.title: The failure-mode table misses a stray `score:` line in the rationale
findings.description:
The new prompt shape puts free-form `## Rationale` prose before the `score:` line. `_SCORE_RE` matches any line that starts with `score:`, and the first match wins. If the model writes a provisional "Score: 90" while reasoning and then a final `score: 72`, the parser takes 90. That can produce a wrong `PASS` with no warning logged. This path is new in this slice, because the rationale-first layout is this slice's addition, but the failure-mode table does not list it.

**Fix:** Add a row for this case. Handle it in the prompt: allow exactly one `score:` line, and require rationale lines to use only the `- <criterion> (<n>):` form. Add a test that a stray earlier `score:` line is treated as a known limitation, or say what detects it.

findings.title: The data-flow example uses the wrong pass floor
findings.description: The data-flow example applies `pass_floor(78)` to `judge.slice-vs-arch`. The threshold table (lines 223-226) and walkthrough step 1 give that template 82; 78 belongs to `judge.tasks-vs-slice`. Under the real floor, a score of 82 still passes, but only just, and anyone writing tests from the example could pick up the wrong value.

findings.title: Judges are identified by the `judge:` block, not the template name
findings.description: The design follows the architecture's "a judge is a review template" principle and slice 301's dispatch rule. Only `is_judge` drives behaviour; the `judge.` prefix is just a readable label. This is consistent with the project rule against using user-visible labels as logic.

findings.title: Explicit `TEMPLATE_INPUTS` entries instead of falling back by prefix
findings.description: The registry in `template_inputs.py` is keyed by exact template name, and unknown names are silently ignored. Two explicit entries are therefore needed. Rejecting a prefix-stripping fallback is the right call, and the change is the smallest one that works.

findings.title: Missing-input failure is caught and observable
findings.description: The claimed path checks out in the code. Missing required inputs raise `KeyError` in `ReviewAction._review()`. `execute()` catches it and `_exception_result` re-looks-up the template, giving `verdict="UNKNOWN"` with judge provenance. This keeps the architecture's no-silent-pass commitment for the new registry entries.

findings.title: Thresholds are set per template and lean toward escalation
findings.description: Defaults live in the template YAML and can be overridden per step through slice 301's mechanism. They sit above 301's module defaults (75/50), and the floor is higher where the ground truth is more open to interpretation. This matches the architecture's "template-level config with step-level override, default conservative" commitment and its "bubble up the hard calls" goal.

findings.title: Scope boundaries and size fit the slice
findings.description: The design correctly leaves cycle conventions to slice 303, gate composition to slice 304, and multi-sample judging to Future Work 1. Apart from the items above, its size fits a 2/5-effort, data-only slice: there are no extra mechanisms or speculative configuration.
